page: OVHcloud rtx5000-84 is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Cloud GPU family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at 3.3 GHz. The system features 84.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.25 GB per core. For accelerated workloads, it includes three NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs based on the Turing architecture, delivering a combined 48 GB of VRAM. Storage is provided via a 400 GB local SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data reveals strong performance in memory and LLM inference tasks. The Passmark memory score is ranked in the top 25 percent, supported by a read-only small block memory bandwidth of 990.44 GB/sec. Large block memory write bandwidth is relatively weaker at 25.38 GB/sec. In LLM inference tests, the server achieves top-tier performance, processing 1827.36 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a medium 7B model and 220.48 tokens/sec on a large 70B model. CPU performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1473.0 and a multi-core score of 8459.0.

The server hardware profile presents a tradeoff between high-tier GPU acceleration and average single-threaded CPU performance, as evidenced by a weaker single-threaded gzip compression rate of 23.78 GB/sec. However, the dedicated 16-core Intel Xeon processor and triple GPU configuration make it highly cost-efficient for parallelized compute tasks without requiring the premium of newer-generation GPU architectures. This server is suited for LLM inference, ray tracing, parallelized data processing, and GPU-accelerated rendering workloads.
description: The OVHcloud rtx5000-84 is a KVM-based server in the Cloud GPU family, configured with an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor featuring 16 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz. It is equipped with 84.0 GB of system memory, a 400 GB local SSD, and a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. The server's primary feature is its triple NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPU setup, providing a total of 48 GB of Turing-architecture VRAM. Benchmark results show top-tier performance in LLM inference, reaching 65.53 tokens/sec for text generation on a 7B model, alongside strong Passmark memory scores. However, single-threaded CPU tasks like gzip compression show weaker relative performance. This configuration is well-suited for GPU-accelerated workloads, including machine learning inference, ray tracing, and parallel data processing.
